Democratic incumbent [[Paul Sarbanes]] was re-elected to a fifth term over former [[Howard County, Maryland|Howard County]] police chief Paul Rappaport. == Republican primary == === Candidates === * [[Robin Ficker]], former state delegate from [[Montgomery County, Maryland|Montgomery County]] and perennial candidate * Ross Z. Pierpont * Paul H. Rappaport, former [[Howard County, Maryland|Howard County]] police chief and [[1994 Maryland gubernatorial election|1994 nominee for lieutenant governor]] * [[Rob Sobhani]], [[Georgetown University]] adjunct professor of political economy * [[John Stafford (American politician)|John Stafford]], [[1998 United States Senate election in Maryland#Republican primary|1998 candidate for Senate]] * [[Kenneth R. Timmerman]], journalist covering the American military and [[Middle East]] affairs * Kenneth Wayman === Results === Rappaport won through a [[grassroots]] movement with a plurality of just 23 percent of the vote.[http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=WT&p_theme=wt&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0EB08BD1D7199B56&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM Rappaport to focus on crime in race with Sarbanes], The Washington Times, March 9, 2000 == General election == === Candidates === * [[Paul Sarbanes]], incumbent U.S. senator since 1977 * Paul H. Rappaport, former [[Howard County, Maryland|Howard County]] police chief [[1994 Maryland gubernatorial election|and 1994 nominee for lieutenant governor]]Dianne Feinstein [https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=uvZHAAAAIBAJ&sjid=-u0DAAAAIBAJ&pg=6610,3359985&dq=former+howard+county+police+chief+paul+rappaport&hl=en Primaries kind to incumbents], The Deseret News (Associated Press) – March 8, 2000[https://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/baltsun/access/62795554.html?dids=62795554:62795554&FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Oct+20%2C+2000&author=Jeff+Barker&pub=The+Sun&desc=Senate+rivals+face+off+in+only+TV+debate+Sarbanes+defends+record+of+4+terms+against+Rappaport+accusations&pqatl=google Senate rivals face off in only TV debate Sarbanes defends record of 4 terms against Rappaport accusations] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105093235/http://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/baltsun/access/62795554.html?dids=62795554:62795554&FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Oct+20,+2000&author=Jeff+Barker&pub=The+Sun&desc=Senate+rivals+face+off+in+only+TV+debate+Sarbanes+defends+record+of+4+terms+against+Rappaport+accusations&pqatl=google |date=November 5, 2012 }}.
